correctness.rationale: The exact published complex is reconstructed from its symmetry generators and two facet seeds. Exact binary row reduction gives ranks 105 and 433 for the relevant boundary maps, hence mod-two second-homology dimension 22. Exhaustion of all 1820 four-sets yields 1100 empty tetrahedra, all with nonzero boundary classes; quotient reduction gives exactly 508 classes with multiplicities 1:320, 3:80, 5:108. The minimum-support statement follows from the complete two-skeleton and the unique two-cycle on four vertices. Group-orbit and span claims are recomputed exactly from the same data.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Tightness can force the homology of an induced four-vertex sphere to inject, covering the nonzero part of the statement, but it does not determine whether two different empty tetrahedra represent the same global class. The exact 508-class quotient, multiplicity distribution, orbit decomposition, and spanning statement are therefore not consequences of the broader theorem alone.

value.rationale: The result classifies the globally smallest possible vertex supports for middle homology in the canonical vertex-minimal, three-neighborly K3 triangulation. The exact collision and symmetry spectrum explains how 1100 induced four-vertex spheres encode a 22-dimensional global homology group. This is a natural local-to-global invariant of the minimal model, not an arbitrary finite slice or a routine recomputation of its face vector.
